papers.title: Don't Waste Bits! Adaptive KV-Cache Quantization for Lightweight On-Device LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across reasoning, generation, and decision-making tasks, yet deploying them on mobile, embedded, and edge devices remains particularly challenging. On-device LLM inference is heavily constrained by the memory and bandwidth overhead of the key-value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with context length and often dominates decoding cost. papers.title: TokenDance: Scaling Multi-Agent LLM Serving via Collective KV Cache Sharing
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM applications organize execution in synchronized rounds where a central scheduler gathers outputs from all agents and redistributes the combined context. This All-Gather communication pattern creates massive KV Cache redundancy, because every agent's prompt contains the same shared output blocks, yet existing reuse methods fail to exploit it efficiently.
